source_snapshot.procedure: Connect, remove and replug the BMC shared-port cable; inspect WebUI and `lan print`; check one bound channel, POST BMC display and optional S5 WOL.
source_snapshot.criteria: Same IP/MAC configuration, working network in all three states, and correct DHCP/static display.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO because cable work is physical; it assumes connectivity/configuration remain valid.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED because no removed-state path, topology, POST/WOL scope or DHCP/static matrix is defined.

old_problem: The previous record required an owner to choose between two normal topology outcomes instead of expressing them as explicit supported branches. It also combined retained configuration with path reachability and let an `Optional` WOL note conflict with later collection text.
disposition_reason: Removing a cable always makes that physical shared path unavailable; this is independently observable. The BMC configuration can still persist, and live service may either become unreachable or fail over through a named alternate path depending on the Project SPEC. Those branches provide non-contradictory Expected Results without guessing hardware. DHCP and static are separate runs, POST is a separate visual checkpoint, and WOL remains the source-marked optional subtest requiring explicit selection.
decision_basis: Direct inspection covered XLSX row 825, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2 and historical record.
The exact shared/NC-SI mux and alternate path are OEM/project topology, not generic IPMI behavior; the test therefore binds them from the approved port/channel map.

IPMI LAN configuration reads can demonstrate stored channel/IP/MAC state but cannot prove traffic used a particular unplugged or failover path; independent switch/link and fresh transaction evidence are required.
ED physical-operation rules keep cabling human-owned, while ED-36 permits addresses, channels and supported-failover mode as Project Configuration.

test_case.test_name: Verify shared-NIC binding, configuration persistence and topology-correct behavior across connect/remove/replug
test_case.purpose: Verify the exact BMC shared-NIC path and one-bound-channel identity in connected, cable-removed and reconnected states for separate static and DHCP configurations, distinguish stored configuration from actual path reachability, verify BMC IP display at POST, and run S5 WOL only when explicitly selected.
required_package: Approved chassis shared-port/host-NIC/NC-SI/dedicated path, IPMI channel, switch port/VLAN and MAC map
Branch selection: no-failover or named supported failover, with expected active path/channel and failback
Separate static IP and DHCP lease/reacquisition expectations plus reachability/recovery deadlines
Independent local/OOB observer not dependent on the shared cable under test
POST display requirement; optional WOL package only if selected, including S5 method, wake MAC/source, timeout and final power state
test_case.test_command: For static and DHCP as independent restored runs, operator traces and connects the exact shared cable. Capture fresh WebUI/IPMI channel/IP/MAC data, switch link/MAC learning and client transactions. Operator removes only that cable. Confirm its switch/PHY link is down, use the independent observer to prove configuration persistence, and apply the selected branch: no-failover requires shared-path reachability loss; named failover requires fresh transactions attributed to the specified alternate path/channel. Replug and verify shared-link and service recovery/failback with unchanged identity. At an approved boot, visually correlate POST BMC IP. Execute S5 WOL only as a separately approved optional phase.
test_case.expected_result: In each address-mode run, connected and replugged states use the approved shared path, one intended bound channel and correct MAC/IP. During removal the shared link is down and stored configuration remains correct; reachability is absent for no-failover or continues only over the documented alternate path for failover. Replug meets the recovery/failback deadline without duplicate address or extra binding. POST shows the expected BMC IP. Optional WOL has its own selected result and cannot affect the primary verdict when not selected.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires both static and DHCP state matrices, physical/link proof, path-attributed fresh transactions, exact channel/MAC/IP and recovery evidence plus POST display. Cached UI values alone do not pass reachability. FAIL includes traffic over an unexplained path, wrong channel/MAC/IP, duplicate address/loop, missing expected failover or unexpected reachability in no-failover mode, failed reacquisition/failback or lost management recovery. WOL is PASS/FAIL only if explicitly selected; otherwise record NOT SELECTED, not silently passed.
safety_gate: Qualified human performs cable removal/reconnection after tracing port, switch and recovery path
Never use the cable under test as the only observer and never infer path from an IP response
Isolate the management network; prevent loops, duplicate IP and accidental production/uplink removal
Restore between static and DHCP runs; do not change address mode without local recovery
No S5/power/WOL action without separate approval; no automatic retry on loss or unintended wake
expected_evidence: Physical/logical topology, serial identity and branch selection
Per-state cable/link/switch/VLAN/MAC-learning and channel/IP/MAC records for static and DHCP
Fresh path-bound WebUI/IPMI/HTTPS/ping transaction evidence and DHCP lease history
Human POST photo tied to the same chassis and expected BMC IP
If selected: S5 entry, magic packet source/target, wake timing and restored power state
Final cable/address/path state and BMC/host health
test_case.recovery: On wrong cable, loop, duplicate address, unexplained responder or management loss, stop; reconnect the traced shared cable, restore the approved switch/VLAN and saved address mode using local/OOB access, and verify exact serial/MAC identity. Do not trigger WOL or retry recabling automatically.

source_conflict.preserved_original_conflict: Master requires network operation after removing the shared cable and repeats optional WOL as an after-test check.
source_conflict.resolution: Separate configuration health from the unplugged path and bind reachability to a documented failover/no-failover branch; preserve WOL as an explicitly selected optional phase.

blocked.reason: The test now has valid branch-specific oracles; topology, addresses and deadlines are Project Configuration.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Shared/alternate path and channel map, failover branch, static/DHCP values/deadlines, observer path, POST expectation and optional WOL package.

external_authorities.title: Intel IPMI v2.0 Specification
external_authorities.use: Provides standard LAN channel/configuration semantics; physical shared-NIC mux and failover remain OEM/project behavior.
